anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L1 task requires depth-sorted 3D selection, frontmost raycasting, rotation, mining blockers and targets, and active hazard/support/durability checks. Bandaged Rose Window at depth 1 is a 2D visible reference/current comparison with two state-dependent disc turns and no 3D occlusion, hazard, durability, or continuous physics. This supports the rose's low end being comparable to a low-level task, but does not make the current depth-4 profile an L1 task.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L3 task has 50 ms physics ticks, momentum/friction, walls and wells, ordered lamps, and a closed-loop control trajectory. Bandaged Rose Window has no time-evolving state or physical recovery: each accepted sixth-turn is discrete and the whole rose remains visible. Its depth-3/4 profiles can require more exact state-dependent planning than a trivial static match, but they do not inherit the tilt board's temporal-control burden. The comparison supports a provisional mid-level placement only by a different difficulty dimension.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L4 task combines an 18x11 warehouse route, five face gates, 48-105 roll limits, orientation changes, and scanner-dependent hidden orientation memory. Bandaged Rose Window at depth 4 has ten state-dependent turns and full-handle precision, but all rose pieces and the reference remain visible, with no route geometry, hidden orientation, or scanner reveals. It is therefore not clearly harder than Blind Dice Courier; keeping it in the same provisional named bucket is defensible for its planning depth, while the burdens are materially different.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L5 task has a 5x5 board in which each valid swap changes the next board through multi-wave cascades/refills, while the agent must hit an exact score and respect forbidden cells. Bandaged Rose Window's depth-5 profile has a longer 14-turn dependent permutation path, but one visible arrangement goal, no cascade arithmetic, no forbidden terminal accounting, and no hidden changing inventory. The comparison supports depth 5 as the rose's highest relative profile but does not prove that it matches the approved global L5 burden; it also supports keeping the current depth-4 baseline below this anchor on interacting-variable complexity.

visible_baseline_solution: A screenshot-only agent sees a solved reference rose, the current stained-glass rose, and three overlapping six-slot discs containing colored pieces with shape/motif cues. It must match the current pieces to the reference, select a disc and direction, and track the resulting arrangement because a successful sixth-turn changes later legal moves. In Simplified mode it presses one of six labelled disc-direction buttons; in Full mode it drags the visible brass handle around the selected disc far enough to cross the angular threshold. Refused turns are silent and leave the current state unchanged, so controlled probing may be needed to infer the overlap rule. It repeats until the exact solved arrangement is visible and presses SEAL. The browser and replay grader require the correct input source, contiguous before/after states, legal turn physics, and the solved final tuple; the private solver route is not part of the screenshot-only task.

baseline_judgment.rationale: The current explicit baseline activates scramble_depth 10, an exact breadth-first distance from the solved rose. Successful turns alter the overlapping-disc state and hence future legal actions, so this is more than ten independent repetitions. It lacks the temporal physics of Gyroscopic Tilt Board, hidden route state of Blind Dice Courier, and multi-variable cascade accounting of Exact-Change Candy Cascade. A provisional L4 placement is plausible, but source supports relative ordering more strongly than absolute calibration.

findings.affected_configurations: All five difficulty profiles in both interaction modes
findings.claim: The generated optimal_distance is not enforced as an exact route length or maximum successful-turn budget.
findings.causal_explanation: The grader limits the transcript to 200 events and checks each event's physics plus the final solved state, but does not compare successful-turn count with optimal_distance. The source test constructs the optimal solution, appends two extra legal turns, and still expects grading to pass. Depth remains the minimum generation distance and still distinguishes profiles, but a solver can take legal detours.

evidence.explanation: The grader checks a maximum event count, replay consistency, totals and the final solved state; it does not enforce optimal_distance.
The source-level test appends two legal turns after the solution and asserts that grading still passes.
optimal_distance and solution_moves are exported in the contract/truth, but this does not impose a route constraint.

findings.recommended_action: If exact shortest-path depth is intended as a work limit, enforce a successful-turn/action budget or remove that claim; otherwise document depth as generation-only and retain the current profile ordering.

concise_summary: Keep the implemented difficulty-4/full baseline. The five profiles are source-distinguished by exact dependent scramble depths 2, 4, 7, 10 and 14, and the two input surfaces preserve the same world and replay physics by source. The placement is provisional rather than calibrated: the task lacks the temporal, hidden-state or cascade interactions of several approved anchors, and optimal path length is not enforced.
limitations: No browser, multi-seed, grader, export, human, VNC or computer-use-agent runtime check was run in this audit; the parent performs runtime checks separately.
No historical pre-controls implementation was available, so historical preservation is not assessable.
Approved-anchor comparisons establish concrete similarities and differences, not empirical conversion between this puzzle's planning/control burden and an absolute L1-L5 score.
The visible overlap rule and usability cost of silent refused turns remain uncertain without human or agent evidence.
